subject: ventures/wildlife-exclusion-bid-calculator
professional: the owner of an independent nuisance-wildlife control / exclusion company who bids raccoon, squirrel, bat and bird jobs (state NWCO licence, trap-check rules, bat maternity moratoria, one-way door practice, multi-year exclusion warranties)

evidence.correctness: Ran a scratch script importing calc.mjs (node w.mjs in the session scratchpad) and recomputed three jobs by hand. (1) The README/page worked example (raccoon, two-story tier 1.7, crew 2, check crew 1, $25 wage + 52% burden, 14 mi / 22 min one way, 3 traps x 12 min, 5 trap days x 1 check x 25 min, 45 ft x 1.4 min x $3.20, 1 door 35 min $45, removal 25 min, decon 250 sq ft at 45 min and $55 per 100, insulation 250 out $1.40 / in $1.90, disposal 90, repair 160, 8% reserve, 14% overhead, 22% margin). Hand: labour rate 25*1.52 = 38; visits 1+1+5+1 = 8; miles 8*2*14 = 224, vehicle 224*0.85 = 190.40; drive hours 3*44*2/60 + 5*44*1/60 = 4.4 + 3.667 = 8.067 h -> $306.53; inspection 45*2/60 = 1.5 h -> $57; seal (45*1.4 + 35 + 25)*1.7 = 209.1 min *2/60 = 6.97 h -> $264.86; trap 3*12*2/60 + 5*25/60 = 3.283 h -> $124.77; decon 112.5*2/60 = 3.75 h -> $142.50; labour 895.66; materials 144+45+21+137.5+825+90+160 = 1422.50; direct 2508.56; reserve 0.08*(264.86+144+45) = 36.31; overhead 351.20; break-even 2896.07; bid 2896.07/0.78 = 3712.91; gap vs $395 = 2501.07. Tool: identical on every line (laborCost 895.66, directCost 2508.56, breakEvenPrice 2896.07, price 3712.91, shortfall 2501.07). (2) Bat job, lift tier 2.4, 90 ft, 3 doors, 400 sq ft decon, no traps, no insulation, 0% reserve, proposed $2,400: hand 3 visits, 84 mi ($71.40), drive 4.4 h ($167.20), seal (126+105+25)*2.4 = 614.4 min *2/60 = 20.48 h ($778.24), decon 6 h ($228), materials 288+135+220+90+350+160 = 1243, direct 2544.84, BE 2901.12, bid 3719.38, proposed margin -501.12/2400 = -20.88%. Tool: all equal; maternity flag true for July, warrantyWithoutReserve true. (3) Ground-tier seal labour: 123 min *2/60*38 = 155.80, as the article says. The arithmetic engine is right for what it computes. Two wrong numbers a user would act on: (a) trap set time. The form label is 'Minutes to place all traps' (index.html:177) and the JSDoc says 'On-site, to place all traps' (calc.mjs:185), but calc.mjs:300 multiplies it by trapsSet. An operator who types 60 minutes to set 10 traps is charged 600 crew-minutes x 2 heads: trap labour $839.17 and bid $4,828.65 instead of $155.17 and $3,828.95 (ran both: trapsSet 10 x trapSetMinutes 60 vs 6). The worked example itself silently uses the per-trap reading (3 x 12 = 36 min; with 12 min total the trap labour would be $94.37, not $124.77). (b) what-to-charge-for-wildlife-exclusion.html:98 says dropping insulation turns the $3,712.91 bid 'into a $2,700 bid'; the tool gives $2,507.14 (BE 1955.57) with insulation zeroed, and naive subtraction gives $2,887.91, so $2,700 matches neither. Capped at 2 for a wrong number on a labelled input.
evidence.completeness: README / page / JSON-LD featureList items checked: visit count from inspection, install, trap checks and removal (works, case 1); drive time and mileage on every visit (works); separate trap-check crew (works, test 10 and mutation); height multiplier on exclusion only (works, cases 1-3); linear-foot exclusion, one-way doors and removal trip (works); decon per 100 sq ft, insulation, disposal, repair (works); reserve on warranted work only (works); overhead and margin, price per crew hour, proposed-price check (works, case 2); flat-fee gap (works); five flags (each fires: ran trapsWithoutChecks with 0 checks -> true, maternity bat/July -> true, warrantyWithoutReserve -> true; doors/untrapped covered by tests); printable proposal and share link (proposal.test.mjs and share.test.mjs pass). Not working: (1) the form hint 'Species sets the starting footage and decides whether this job has trapping in it at all' (index.html:147) is false. SPECIES_PRESETS carry exclusionLinearFeet, deconSquareFeet and oneWayDoors (calc.mjs:84-126), but index.html only uses the presets to fill the select (index.html:390); grep finds no handler that applies them, so choosing Bats keeps 3 traps, 5 trap days and 45 ft, and the user gets the untrapped-species flag for a value the page set itself. (2) The 'The inspection is billed (unchecked = free)' checkbox (index.html:168) does nothing: calc.mjs:241 reads inspectionBillable and never uses or returns it, although the JSDoc (calc.mjs:180-182) says it 'makes the free inspection line visible'. The README does not mention the proposal or share features the page has. I did not drive the page in a browser; the page wiring was checked by reading index.html and by page.test.mjs.
evidence.verification: Ran: cd ventures/wildlife-exclusion-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs' -> tests 175, pass 175, fail 0 (also bare `node --test` as the README says: 175/175). Seeded mutation 1, calc.mjs:310 trap-check drive charged to crewSize instead of trapCheckCrewSize: 4 failures (test 10 'trap checks are charged to the tech who actually goes', 42, 45, 165 article/table figures). Mutation 2, calc.mjs:336 lift rental charged on every tier plus calc.mjs:356 trapsWithoutChecks condition '=== 0' -> '< 0': 6 failures (15 'a lift is charged only on the tier that needs one', 26 'traps set ... no checks budgeted is flagged', 42, 43, 45, 165). Mutation 3, calc.mjs:300 changed to the label's meaning (trapSetMinutes total, not per trap): 3 failures, all article-figure tests (42, 45, 165) and no unit test of trap-set time, i.e. the tests pin the behaviour that contradicts the label. Each reverted with git checkout -- calc.mjs; git status --short then printed nothing. Gaps: no test that the species select applies its preset, none for inspectionBillable, none that warrantyYears changes anything, and the article's '$2,700' is not covered by the 'every currency figure' test (it only matches cents-precision figures). The figure-in-prose tests are a real strength.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (all 450 lines), the script block of index.html, usage.mjs, page.test.mjs head, and the headers of proposal.mjs and share.mjs. calculateBid is one 210-line function but plainly staged (visits, labour, vehicle, materials, reserve, flags) with a named number() validator and specific error messages; pure, frozen presets, no dependencies. Defects: dead input inspectionBillable (calc.mjs:241) and dead preset fields exclusionLinearFeet/deconSquareFeet/oneWayDoors (calc.mjs:84-126, never read anywhere); JSDoc contradicting code for trapSetMinutes (calc.mjs:185 vs :300); validation accepts non-integer crew size (crewSize 1.5 priced $3,458.69) and scheduledMonth 6.5 (silently disables the maternity flag); trapDays*checks is Math.round-ed (2.5 days -> 3 visits) without saying so; proposal.mjs is byte-identical (md5 f3797c40...) to 121 other ventures' copies, a copied engine by design that will drift.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer present and specific on index.html:347 and all three extra pages (vs-a-flat-395-removal-fee.html:124, vs-pestpac.html:93, what-to-charge:135); 'no network requests' backed (calc.mjs/usage.mjs have no fetch; usage.mjs:8 honours DNT and GPC); worked-example figures in README and article backed by calc (tests 42-45, 165 and my recomputation); PestPac described as a WorkWave field-service platform with a non-affiliation note (consistent with my recollection; vendor site not loaded). SEO: the source files use placeholders, sitemap.xml and robots.txt name https://example.invalid/..., canonicals are relative ('./', './vs-pestpac.html'), llms.txt names the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host; platform/pages/build.mjs:5522 rewriteOrigin rewrites both hosts at build. Loaded live with curl: https://marisstella.app/wildlife-exclusion-bid-calculator/ 200 with canonical and og:url absolute on marisstella.app; live llms.txt links all point at https://marisstella.app/...; live per-venture sitemap.xml has absolute marisstella.app locs (extensionless) and the root robots.txt names https://marisstella.app/sitemap.xml, which lists the venture sitemap; the three .html pages 307 to extensionless URLs that return 200. So the served SEO is correct; the committed files are not self-contained (a reader of the repo sees example.invalid and github.io), and vs-pestpac.html:12 og:url is example.invalid in source. Unbacked: 'Species sets the starting footage' (index.html:147), 'unchecked = free' inspection (index.html:168), 'Minutes to place all traps' (index.html:177), and the '$2,700 bid' (what-to-charge:98).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job an NWCO owner would price first: a raccoon in a two-story attic with five days of trapping. Filled from the defaults it produces a defensible, line-by-line bid, a visit count to show the customer, a flat-fee comparison and a printable proposal, which is the real job. Then a bat exclusion: choosing Bats changes nothing but the label, so the user must zero traps, trap days and checks by hand, re-enter footage and doors, and read the untrapped-species flag the page itself caused. An operator who reads the trap-set label literally and enters total minutes on a 6-10 trap job over-bids by hundreds to a thousand dollars and loses it. Missing items an owner prices on most jobs: per-animal handling/euthanasia or disposal fees, a minimum job charge, multiple exclusion materials (hardware cloth vs. vent guards vs. chimney cap as unit items rather than one $/ft), door-monitoring visits, and a lift charged once although the removal trip is at the same height. Usable with care for a raccoon/squirrel trapping job; not trustworthy as left for bats, birds or many-trap jobs.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard NWCO practice (state trap-check rules, NWCOA/AAWCP-style exclusion work, bat maternity moratoria). Sound: trap checks counted as paid round trips; bats and birds excluded not trapped; one-way door removal trip; height as a multiplier on exclusion labour only; reserve on warranted work; maternity-season flag presented as a prompt, months 5-8 for bats close to the common state bat-exclusion moratoria (roughly late May to mid August, from recollection, not loaded). Departures: (1) the warranty reserve ignores warrantyYears (ran 1 year and 10 years: both $36.31; calc.mjs:346), so a 10-year warranty, common in exclusion sales, is reserved like a 1-year one; (2) the 'Skunks, groundhogs, opossums' preset has maternitySeasonRisk false (calc.mjs:122-123), though skunk and groundhog young under decks and sheds in spring are the classic case where a one-way door traps kits; (3) birds are flagged only for nesting months with no mention that most native birds and active nests are federally protected (Migratory Bird Treaty Act; only house sparrow, starling and feral pigeon are generally excluded), which is what an owner checks first on a bird job; (4) no rabies-vector / bat-exposure handling or histoplasmosis PPE distinction for guano versus raccoon latrine (decon is one rate); (5) no line for what happens to a trapped animal (euthanasia or relocation rules vary by state, many prohibit relocation) or per-animal charges, which is how many operators actually bill the trapping half.

defects.what: Trap set time is labelled and documented as total minutes for all traps but multiplied by the trap count; 10 traps at 60 total minutes bids $4,828.65 instead of $3,828.95. Tests pin the per-trap behaviour.

Species presets (footage, decon area, one-way doors, and 'decides whether this job has trapping') are never applied by the page; choosing Bats keeps 3 traps and 5 trap days, contradicting the form hint.
'The inspection is billed (unchecked = free)' checkbox is dead: inspectionBillable is read and never used or returned.
Warranty reserve does not depend on warranty length; 1-year and 10-year warranties reserve the same $36.31.
Skunk/groundhog/opossum preset has no maternity-season risk, though spring young under decks are the standard one-way-door hazard.
Article says dropping insulation makes the bid 'a $2,700 bid'; the tool gives $2,507.14 (naive subtraction $2,887.91). Not covered by the figure tests.
Bird jobs carry no Migratory Bird Treaty Act prompt; lift rental charged once although the device-removal trip is at the same height.

verdict: The cost engine is arithmetically right: three jobs recomputed by hand (raccoon worked example, bat lift job, ground-tier seal) match calc.mjs to the cent, 175 tests pass and three seeded mutations were each caught. The page around it is not finished to a professional bar. The 'Minutes to place all traps' input is multiplied by the trap count, so an operator who reads the label over-bids a many-trap job by up to a thousand dollars; the species picker that the form says 'sets the starting footage and decides whether this job has trapping' changes nothing but the label; the 'free inspection' checkbox is dead; the warranty reserve ignores the warranty's length; and a wildlife owner would expect skunk/groundhog maternity, migratory-bird and animal-disposition handling that is absent. Live SEO on marisstella.app is correct (absolute canonical, sitemap and llms.txt after the build rewrite). It does not meet the bar: correctness, claims and the median are 2.
